answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can cap what brand-new identities may do and let reputation grow only through verifiable completed work. Like an ocean fed by countless small streams, trust accumulates drop by drop: each finished task adds a little, while a fresh identity starts as a faint ember with almost no spending power. Creating a nebula of fake agents gains nothing, because every fake must slowly earn the same costly history before it can move real value, so an attacker pays in time and compute for each identity.
